title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F20
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 41 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)
EO science strategy and scientific literature

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

items.question: Search ArXiv for papers on ERA5 2-metre temperature trends over the Mediterranean. Based on the study region and reference period in the papers, download ERA5 2m temperature to provide a concrete dataset for the analysis.

answers.text:

The study arXiv:2608.00063v1 specifically utilized ERA5 reanalysis from 1950 to 2024 to analyze these warming rates and spatial persistence.

• Region: Mediterranean (approx. 30°N to 46°N, 6°W to 36°E)
• Period: 1950–2024
• File Path: med_temp_1950_2024.nc

items.question: Geocode the city of Aral, Kazakhstan. Retrieve a suitable Sentinel-2 true-colour observation covering the area during July 2023. Assess the current Aral Sea shoreline, describe visible evidence of environmental change, and explain how the observation could be combined with historical data to quantify shoreline retreat.

answers.text:
Based on the Sentinel-2 true-color image of Aral, Kazakhstan, taken in July 2023, the following observations can be made:

1. Current Aral Sea Shoreline
The image clearly shows the remnants of the Aral Sea, which has drastically shrunk over the decades. The visible shoreline is now a narrow, fragmented strip of water, surrounded by vast expanses of dry, cracked earth. The water body appears to be divided into smaller, isolated sections, with the largest remaining portion being a small, elongated lake near the center of the image.

2. Visible Evidence of Environmental Change
• Desertification: The surrounding landscape is predominantly barren and arid, with large areas of exposed, dry land indicating significant water loss.
• Salt Flats and Evaporation Pits: The image reveals numerous salt flats and evaporation pits, which are characteristic of the Aral Sea's drying process. These areas appear as white or light-colored patches, indicating the accumulation of salt deposits left behind as water evaporated.
• Fragmentation of Water Bodies: The Aral Sea is no longer a single, continuous body of water but is instead fragmented into smaller, disconnected sections, which is a clear sign of its severe shrinkage.

3. Combining with Historical Data to Quantify Shoreline Retreat
To quantify the extent of shoreline retreat, the current Sentinel-2 image can be compared with historical satellite imagery from previous decades (e.g., 1980s, 1990s, or early 2000s). By overlaying these images, one can:
• Measure the Distance: Use geographic information system (GIS) tools to measure the distance between the current shoreline and historical shorelines.
• Calculate the Area Lost: Determine the area of water that has been lost over time by comparing the extent of the water body in the current image with historical images.
• Analyze Trends: Identify trends in the rate of shoreline retreat, which can help in understanding the environmental impact and potential future scenarios.

This approach would provide a comprehensive understanding of the environmental changes in the Aral Sea region and highlight the severity of the ecological crisis.

Current Aral Sea Shoreline
The image reveals a starkly diminished Aral Sea, with the remaining water body appearing as a fragmented, shallow remnant. The shoreline is irregular and fragmented, with significant portions of the former sea bed now exposed as dry, cracked earth. The visible water areas are small and isolated, indicating severe desiccation.

Visible Evidence of Environmental Change
1. Shoreline Retreat: The most prominent evidence is the dramatic retreat of the shoreline. The exposed seabed, now covered in salt flats and dry sediment, stretches far beyond the current waterline, indicating a substantial loss of water volume over time.
2. Salt Flats and Evaporation Pits: The image shows extensive salt flats and evaporation pits, which are characteristic of a drying lake. These features are visible as white and light-colored patches surrounding the remaining water bodies.
3. Fragmentation of Water Bodies: The Aral Sea is no longer a single, contiguous body of water. Instead, it is fragmented into smaller, isolated pools, which is a clear sign of ecological degradation.
4. Human Impact: The image also shows human settlements and infrastructure near the remaining water bodies, highlighting the impact of human activity on the region's environment.

Quantifying Shoreline Retreat with Historical Data
The Sentinel-2 image from July 2023 can be combined with historical satellite imagery to quantify shoreline retreat. By comparing the current shoreline with historical images from previous decades (e.g., 1990s or 2000s), one can measure the rate and extent of shoreline recession. This can be done using GIS software to digitize the shoreline in both the current and historical images and calculate the area lost over time. The data can then be used to model the rate of retreat and predict future changes, providing valuable insights for environmental management and policy-making.

This analysis underscores the severe environmental degradation of the Aral Sea and highlights the urgent need for conservation and restoration efforts.

4. Validation:
